utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Mr. Vanderpuye, is the next witness ready? Which is in fact not the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon to you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, and everybody. The next witness is ready.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. He should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Janc. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: A long time ago, you have already been here in this trial. And, therefore, I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony is still -- applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And I understood the Prosecution that we are back in examination-in-chief. And it's up to you, Mr. Vanderpuye, to examine the witness. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise for the delay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We have to interrupt your cross-examination for some more direct examination as you know. And what we plan to do today is to introduce seven video-clips during the course of your testimony, as you also know. Have you had an opportunity to review these videos?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. I have had the opportunity to review all these videos. Some of them during -- as a member of the team of the Srebrenica investigation team, investigative team, and some of them even upon first arrival at the OTP so in 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Just for the record, Your Honours, these videos - and I will show them - are P236, 65 ter 1396, 65 ter 5508, P681, 65 ter 2436, 5499, and 5498. Mr. Janc, in the course of preparing for your testimony here today and -- have you had an opportunity to determine the circumstances under which the Prosecution came into possession of this video material? Just generally, and we'll get into it more specifically a little bit further on.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's also true. Generally, I got familiarized myself from -- with the -- with the background of information on how the Prosecution obtained these videos, from which sources, when, and also some authentic issues have been taken into consideration when preparing for this testimony here. So, in general term, yes, I am aware --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us just --

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- generally what types of documents or material you reviewed in relation to that effort.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, since most of the stuff, we will be viewing during my testimony is -- was obtained by the authorities -- official authorities in the former Yugoslavia, in particular Serbian authorities and BiH authorities, and they provided us with the accompanying documentation on how they obtained these videos in first place, from which places, from which locations, from which individuals. And this is first set of documents I have reviewed. Then for some of the videos, we -- there is particular one video which we obtained from -- from a confidential source, and in relation to that one, I -- I reviewed information or statement which was provided by this confidential source in relation to that video. Also, a declaration from investigator was drafted in relation to that video, so this is the third source of this documentation which I reviewed. And also, different statements from -- from individuals involved, involved or -- yeah, which we can see on the videos, and we'll discuss every -- every single one in detail when we -- we watch them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right then. What I'd like to do then is I'd like to get started, and we have a video which we have indicated here as 12 July in Vlasenica. Are you familiar with that one?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And this is our first video on our list today which we will reviewing, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And before we play it, can you just give us a little bit of context. Tell us who is featured in it and perhaps you can tell us a little bit about when the events depicted in it occurred.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What we will be watching today is just an excerpt of the longer video which was -- which the OTP obtained in 2009, so we have just made a video-clip of some portion from that video. We will see mainly the speech of the General Milenko Zivanovic, who was at that time still the Drina Corps commander. And it is about the celebration of the Saint Patrons' Day on the 12th of July 1995, and this celebration is taking place at the Zvonko Bajagic's apartment in Vlasenica. Zvonko Bajagic, he was a second lieutenant at that time for Drina Corps logistic -- logistic department, and he has been hosting this lunch. And before the lunch took place, General Zivanovic has made a speech regarding the recent events in relation to the fall of Srebrenica. Also, we will see on the video Zvonko Bajagic and the priest Vasilije Kacavenda. At the dinner there were also other -- other members of the VRS involved, present, and we can discuss this later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I thank you very much for that introduction. I guess we'd like to go ahead and play the video now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we do that, let me put a question to the witness, please. You have said we made a video-clip of some portion of that video. Could you tell us a little bit about the source from where you were able to obtain this video? If that is possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can, and when preparing for this testimony, the plan was that we discuss the sources for each and single one, every single video when we reviewed the video, but can I tell you about the source already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It would be helpful for the Chamber but I think for the other participants as well to know in advance the source of the single video we are looking at.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No problem. I will do it that way. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay, Mr. Janc, could you tell us then specifically about the source of the video that we're about to see.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The OTP obtained this video from the Serbian authorities in March of 2009, exactly on 27 of March 2009, and it came -- it came from the Serbian MUP, which seized this VHS tape during the search conducted on 4th of December, 2008, at the premises of the General Ratko Mladic's son apartment in Belgrade. And, yes, on 27 of March, 2009, our investigator Tomasz Blaszczyk went down to Belgrade and obtained this particular videotape from Serbian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could just show you 65 ter 6577.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to say for the record which Serb authority are meant, whether those in the Republika Srpska or those in Serbia, because there are several Serb authorities. So I would like that to be clear for the record, and there are several MUPs too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Tolimir, I am of the same opinion. That would been one of my questions as well. Could you clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I actually have the document which I will show Mr. Janc, Mr. President. I think the document speaks for itself and will clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The first document that I have, though, on the screen, and that is 65 ter 6577, can you tell us what that is, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is information report which was prepared by my colleague investigator Blaszczyk in relation to the -- how he received this -- this -- this tape from the Serbian authorities. And we can see here that he was in Belgrade and that he received this stuff from the Office of the Serbian War Crime Prosecutor. So these are authorities of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I don't -- we don't have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the document number. It was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, Mr. President. It was 65 ter 6577.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I believe we don't have a translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And we have to correct the number on page 5, line 14, then there is a wrong number recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For this document, you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes. To the witness, and maybe to Mr. Vanderpuye eventually, page 5, line 11: "And, yes, on 27th of March, 2009, our investigator Tomasz Blaszczyk went down to Belgrade and obtained this particular tape from Serbian authorities." My question to you is what is your connection, Witness to this document. Since it's the other investigator who went to collect it from Serbia -- Serbian authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps to this document I have no direct connection, but before that we obtained from Serbian authorities the electronic version of the documents and VHS tapes which were digitalised by the Serbian authorities in the meantime, and we received this electronic material at the end of the actually -- in the middle of March 2009, and we reviewed all this stuff initially here which was on DVDs, and we have made a list of the stuff of the highest priority for the Office of the Prosecution, and that's why Thomas Blaszczyk went down to Belgrade and collect initial sets of documents and VHS tapes from Serbian War Crime Prosecutor's office. Later on, they provided us, I mean Serbian authorities, with all the other additional stuff which was also seized during the search of General Mladic's apartment in Belgrade. So in this sense I would -- because we will see on the page which follows that Mr. Blaszczyk explains what -- which tape -- which tapes he received or he obtained at this point in time, and I can say that I reviewed all these tapes, and I familiarised myself as a member of the Srebrenica team, so that's how I see the connection to this particular document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is just, in my view, to be meant to show the chain of custody how did we get the material from the source and how we handled it here at the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If we could just go briefly to the first page of this document. I see that we're on the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On the first page of the document, and I did note that we didn't have a translation of it but I wanted to read the header into it so that Mr. Tolimir is fully apprised much its contents. It's entitled: "International Criminal Tribunal for the Prosecution of Persons Responsible for Serious Violations of International Law Committed in the Territory of the Former Yugoslavia Since 1991." It's an information report. It's dated 1st April 2009. And its subject matter indicates "chain of custody of the documents (notebooks and VHS tapes received from the Office of the War Crimes Prosecutor in Belgrade Serb)." And in the first paragraph it indicates that on 27 March 2009 in Belgrade, as the witness has testified, the following documents were handed over to me, that's Mr. Blaszczyk, which were seized by the Serbian MUP on 4 December 2008 in several premises used by Ratko Mladic and his family. On the second page, if we can go briefly, I think the witness can then explain what he was referring to about the circumstances or the materials, I should say, relevant to the videotape which is P236 that we're go doing play that Mr. Blaszczyk received. So if you could just direct us to the paragraphs that concern the videotapes that we're going to see, beginning the one that we will start with, P236, given the date of 12 July 1995. Do you see that reference in this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that on this page. It's actually paragraph 8 or the last paragraph on this page. And you can see, for example, what -- what -- what is the content on the tape itself. And here is written everything what was on that tape. And as I already mentioned, we have -- we have just extracted the portion which we are interested in, which is -- yeah. You can see the fourth line in this paragraph where it says "General Zivanovic made a speech related to the liberation of Srebrenica." He said that at 1620 hours on the previous day, they put Serbian flag on Serbian church in Srebrenica. And then later on you -- you have explained what other contents on this same VHS tapes are. Towards the end of this paragraph, it is the fourth line from the end, you can see the sentence which starts: "This VHS tape was marked by Serbian MUP with number 97." On the tape -- on the tape's label is written "A-54." And on the tape's box: "Srebrenica, Snimljeno, 12th of July, 1995 ..." and so on. So why is this important? Because we have also received from -- from the authorities of the Republic of Serbia the report about the content on the -- on the videos. They have also reviewed all this material and they have made, prepared a report on what can be seen on these videos, and since many of those videotapes have been seized during the search at the Mladic's premises, they were, I think, around 100 tapes. They were marked by these specific numbers. So this one was marked as number 97, and -- yeah, you can see from the -- from the -- from the text here itself that it is -- it is dated 12th of July. The events which are on the tape are taking place on 12 of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: While we're on the subject, I also wanted to refer you to paragraph 7, and at paragraph 7 refers to a tape containing clips of a military parade and it says here of setting up the manoeuvre brigade of the Drina Corps. This is also a tape that we're planning to show. Did you have an opportunity to review this entry in Mr. Blaszczyk's information report and what can you -- if you have, what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I also reviewed this part of his report, and also the VHS tape itself, and, yeah, when the reviewing this paragraph I spotted one mistake Mr. Blaszczyk has made, and it is in relation to the tape number, which is here number 28, but the correct number should be 29. So, the VHS tape number 28 is related to the tape under paragraph 6, the first paragraph on this page, and you can see that he marked it or he put number 28 also for that tape in that paragraph. So here it should be 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to have the witness shown 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 6577 will be Exhibit P1016 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I would like to the witness, please, shown 65 ter 6578.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to correct line 24. It's not -- the words "pending translation" are missing. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. We're go to have to go to page -- I think it should be 22 in the B/C/S. Anyway, it should be 65 ter ending 7841 -- I'm sorry, ERN ending 7841. That's good. That's fine right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we can go -- can go to the next page, please, in the B/C/S. One page following. And I think we'll be on the same page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand we need the translation for 0677-7841. Now I see some head shaking going on over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you able to read this or ...

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can read this, perhaps rather slowly but I know what this document is --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's do it like that. Can you identify for us what this document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: First we should remove the English text because it is nothing related to the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And we do have this English translation because I have seen that one. But this is actually the report that I have been testifying about, dated 3rd of February, 2009, prepared by the Ministry of the Internal Affairs of the Republic of Serbia about the content of the seized material with -- with Ratko Mladic's son apartment, and this index where you can see labelled by numbers has been provided to the OTP on 4th of February, 2009, so the day after this document, and at that time they haven't provided us any -- any of the -- the tapes and any of the stuff which was seized. Just that was information for us on what they -- they seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And if we could go to page -- should be four pages up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could go to page 4 of the translation, it should correspond to the -- to the B/C/S as well. Should be ERN ending 7 -- 7844, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And I would like to make one remark because we can see here DVD marked as certain number. What was done was that all this stuff when it was received or seized and then later on reviewed at the MUP premises, was digitalised, and -- and that's why we see here on DVD instead of VHS tape. So -- but when it says marked with such and such number, this number correspond to the number which was on the VHS tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could just go to the fourth page of the translation, and I think it should correspond -- I think it should be the fourth page also in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I want to direct your attention if I could to item number 20, and we'll catch up in the B/C/S in a moment. I think we have it now. Will you tell us a little bit about item number 20.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the B/C/S is not the -- the correct page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Looks like we may have to go back 20 pages up, I think, in the B/C/S or so. It should be 7844, ERN. Page 26? It's page 26 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Previous page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Previous page. Yep. All right --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we need the English translation back. We had it on this screen. It just disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think we've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thanks very much, Mr. Janc. Can you tell us about item number 20.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see here it says DVD marked 29, so this is the number which would correspond to what I testified before, to paragraph number 7 in Blaszczyk's report. So -- and it says here what is the content of this DVD or actually VHS tape which was seized and that's the video we will be watching today.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If I could just refer you to page number 7 in the translation, which will hopefully correspond to page 28 or 29 in the B/C/S. In any event, I'm going to refer you to item number 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's not the correct page in B/C/S but in English. Please back the English version and one further page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think next page in English. Mr. Vanderpuye asked for item 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's the right page in the English. It's the wrong page in the B/C/S. It should be the next page in the B/C/S, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, the previous page. We need item number 52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I was told that there is no item 52 in the document in B/C/S. There's no page in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, then it appears there's page missing in the uploaded document. All right. Well, I think we can manage through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Basically, can you tell us what item 52 concerns.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Similar as previous one, item 52 concerns to the DVD marked tape 52 and it says here what is -- what was on tape, actually, and we will be watching part of this video as I think the last one in -- in my testimony, and it is about the celebration of new years eve on 13th of January, 1996. And this tape was not taken on 27 of March in Belgrade. Mr. Blaszczyk did not take with him back to The Hague this tape because at that time this wasn't considered as a priority tape, but it was provided to us, the original tape was provided to us, by the authorities of the Republic of Serbia at the beginning of April 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. President, item 52 concerns 65 ter 5498, which is the 13 January 1996 speech. At the bottom of the page in the B/C/S and in the English, it's the second-to-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us about this item?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the VHS tape marked as 97 which we are about to watch in a few minutes, so it is about the Patron's Saint Day, as can you see from the description, on 12th of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would offer this document into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received but the correct compilation of pages should be checked again and, if necessary, uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.text: I just want to show you one other document before we play the video, and it should be very brief. It's 65 ter --

utterances.text: We need the exhibit number first.

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 6578 will be Exhibit P1017.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to have the witness shown briefly 65 ter 6579. We have I believe an English translation beginning where we see the list in the B/C/S in the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us, first of all, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document which accompanying -- which is a -- actually their letter accompanying the original stuff sent to -- to the OTP. Original stuff, I'm referring to -- to the one seized during the search on 4th of December, 2008.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And we can see in the first paragraph there's a reference to 27 March 2009. Does that correspond to your information concerning the materials that were turned over to Mr. Blaszczyk?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if I could, if we could just refer to the last page of this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You just referred, Mr. Vanderpuye, to the first paragraph. We didn't see it in English on the screen, only in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're right, Mr. President. Apparently the very first paragraph and the title of the document itself hasn't been translated. The list that accompanies the inventory was translated and that's what we're seeing now. I'll arrange to have the first page of the document also translated so that we have a complete record of what it is. But, in particular, I was referring the witness to the last page of a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And I just direct your attention to the indication here as to the items received by Tomasz Blaszczyk. You can see how it's spelled there, but did you have an opportunity to review this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have confirmed with Mr. Blaszczyk that in fact he received the materials that are indicated in it?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, he received all this material on that day, which was, I think, 6th of April, 2009, and then he brought it here in The Hague by car.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And do have you personal knowledge of that? I mean, did you acquire that from speaking to him and have you seen the material itself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I talked to him about this stuff, and when this material was here, I was very much involved in reviewing all this stuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, may I add a question. Do you know if there are different copies of this document? Not different but several copies of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. But since I see the original stamp here, I would doubt there is additional -- additional original document.

utterances.text: I put this question to you because I don't see a signature of Mr. Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, are you right. Most probably Mr. Blaszczyk did not sign this copy of it, because this copy was for us, for the OTP, and most probably will find the other original in Belgrade with the War Crime Prosecutor, where he signed this -- on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Was that the normal procedure the OTP followed, that those who have given documents to the OTP received a receipt of these documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed this is quite normal procedure for the OTP. Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Vanderpuye go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would tender this document at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification, pending full translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 6579 will be Exhibit P1018, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: With that, I would like to play the videotape, which is P236. And I understand that the transcripts have been uploaded. And it is a subtitled video, so there shouldn't be a need for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you I just asked to stop the video for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If we could identify the people that are in this video, Mr. Janc, in this frame?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The speaker on the right left-hand side, as I already explained, it is General Milenko Zivanovic; at that time, still the commander of the Drina Corps. Next to it, it's a man in white -- white shirt, I think he was a waiter at that time, just a non-important person for us. So then we have to the -- at the top right corner we just see a little bit of his face, but throughout the video can you see him better. This is Mr. Zvonko Bajagic who is hosting this event. And underneath at the bottom right corner, you can see the priest Vasilije Kacavenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll just play it out and I'll have a couple of other questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And you should indicate where you stopped this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think we have an indication of 40.22.1 on the counter. I'm not sure that it's consistent with the version that we have in e-court. But, for the record anyway, I think this is clear enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 40 minutes, 22.1 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to offer in this -- well, it is in evidence so I won't offer it in but --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We have an indication here, Mr. Janc, of a date of 12 July. Can you tell in the context of this video how that determination was made?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see from the video itself, from the speech of Mr. Zivanovic itself, when he is talking about the liberation of Srebrenica the day before. That's one indication that is indeed happening on 12th of July. And if you look into the entire video, before that we have some ceremony going on in church in Vlasenica, and later on in municipality in Vlasenica. And everything is relation to this Saint Patrons [sic] Day which is also on 12 of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you notice also an indication as to an air attack which occurred, as he puts it, "yesterday"? Does the investigation that you've engaged in in relation to these events, is it consistent with the date of this video being taken on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. There was an air attack on 11th of July. And it's another corroboration.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Does the investigation indicate or, rather, support General Zivanovic's assertion that a flag was raised in Srebrenica on the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's also the case. We have -- we have information documents and also I think intercepts when General Gvero is talking to President Karadzic about this specific issue, about raising the flag on the church in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to go to the next video footage. We are going through this chronologically. But before we do, let me first identify to you so that you know what we are talking about, we have an indicated date of 13 July, 1995, and for the record it's 65 ter 1396. Do you have a familiarity with this particular video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. And I reviewed also this one, and I think this was -- I reviewed that one at the time when it -- it came into our office, and it is a short video-clip of General Ratko Mladic being in Srebrenica town on 13 of July, 1995. First, he gives a short speech in front of the Orthodox church in Srebrenica. Then we have priest which is inside this church, and he indicates that we are on that day, on -- in Srebrenica. So on 13 of July in Srebrenica. And then we have a General Mladic going to meet a Serb woman who returned back to Srebrenica, and he -- he meets her there asking her about -- about the destiny of her husband and kids, and together with him at that spot we'll see there is again Zvonko Bajagic, the same individual who hosted the lunch on the video we just -- we just saw, and also Colonel Petar Salapura. He is also there. He is an intelligence officer of the VRS Main Staff. And as for the background, how we -- we got this video, the OTP made a request for the search to be conducted at the residence of VRS Main Staff press officer, I think at that time he was a colonel, Milutin Milo -- Miladin Milutinovic, sorry. And, indeed, search was conducted by the members of the ministry of internal affairs of the Republika Srpska, Bosnia and Herzegovina, in Banja Luka on 22nd of July, 2009, and during this search, this tape was also seized. Later on, it was handed over by the members of the MUP of the Republika Srpska to the BiH State Court in Sarajevo in Bosnia, who handed over these original tapes to us on 25th of August, 2009. And we digitalised all these tapes with co-operation of the EUFOR forces in Bosnia-Herzegovina and then the original tapes were returned back to the BiH State Court, but what we have got here at -- into our house was just a DVD made of these VHS tapes, and so that's what we have here in evidence. It is actually the DVD which was digitised from these VHS tapes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could just have the witness shown, please, 65 ter 6582.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recognise this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I stop you for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, we have discussed two questions. The first one is a question to the witness: Could you tell us how you were able to identify the people depicted in the -- the last video we have seen? You said this is General Zivanovic; this is the waiter. How did you know that? What is the source of your knowledge about the identification of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can explain. Throughout my work as investigator here for Srebrenica team, I have reviewed many statement, many videos and many -- many other documents, and throughout this investigation, I got familiar of -- got familiar regarding certain individuals, especially, of course, the individuals which are VRS members. So you should always get familiarised as investigator and be interested in who you are seeing on every single video or every single evidence you come across during your investigation. And that was the way how I learnt, although I never personally met General Zivanovic, he was interviewed by the OTP several times. I -- I reviewed his statement and, for example, you can see when the videos or some documents or photos were shown to him where he identifies himself, for example, and also throughout the investigation we interviewed many other peoples, people where they were identifying these people. So that's the source of information, how I know who these people are. For example, for Zvonko Bajagic, for that one, I am -- I got aware first time who this individual is when he testified here for Defence in Popovic case. That was -- although he has been seen on various videos from before, we have never actually identified him before and when he was here, we identified him through these means. So -- yeah. And these are basically, basically the -- the ways how I am able to say who these people are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you confront any person with this video and ask any person; and, if so, whom who can -- could identify the people depicted in the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For this particular video, I cannot say if we confronted anyone with this video. It's possible. But I cannot say from the top -- I would need to check, and I think for -- exactly for these purposes how we identify each and every single one. My colleague investigator Erin Gallagher is preparing right now, who will be testifying about the video stills taken from these videos and where these individuals will be depicted again, and she will, I think, let you know how we identified them, through which -- through which means, through which statement, through which individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You referred to the man sitting on the right side on the video as priest and you mentioned a name. I heard in the video the speaker saying, I am glad that the bishop is with us. How would you explain the difference between bishop and priest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I do apologise. It's -- indeed it's not a priest because according to the church there are several different levels of -- of -- of the church officials, and the priest is, I think, a lower level. But this individual is -- yeah, it can be bishop. It is one from -- from the higher echelon of this church. But I'm not that familiar with the church structure. So he is for sure not just a priest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you saying that every bishop is a priest but not every priest a bishop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do apologise, Your Honour. I don't know the -- the exact differences between them, so I'm afraid I cannot respond to -- to this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, I would like to ask you, because we discussed it among us, why are you showing this video and perhaps the other videos through this witness? What is the relation between this witness and the videos? Perhaps can you elaborate on that a little bit further.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sure, thanks Mr. President. We're showing this sequence of videos through this witness because this witness is an investigator with the Srebrenica trial team, has familiarity with the course of the investigation, the individuals that are depicted in the -- in the videos, the context in which -- or the context that is presented in the videos in relation to the events on the ground, which is within the ken of this witness's expertise, knowledge, and experience, and he has familiarity with the chain of custody concerning these videos which I know is an issue that the Court is interested in and certainly has been interested in with respect to other witnesses. So that's the reason why it's coming in through this witness. Doesn't mean necessarily that it might not come in through other witnesses as well or other witnesses may comment on it, but I think that this witness's familiarity with the investigation, the players that are involved that are depicted in the video, the circumstances that the video is involved, and the context in which the footage -- in which the footage was taken, and ultimately delivered to the Office of the Prosecutor and then developed, analysed and -- and introduced to the Court is within his -- is certainly within his -- within his knowledge and abilities, and that's the reason why it is coming in through him. You may opine, and can I see by the expression on your face, that it might be more appropriate to introduce the videos through other witnesses and I agree that that may be true, but I don't think that that necessarily is the only avenue through which the video can come into this case, and I think as the case develops and as the evidence comes in you will be able to see more clearly why it is that we can -- why it is introduced through this witness and how it's also relevant to other witnesses as they come in. So that, in a nutshell, is -- is our position on it with respect to this witness. It could come in through Mr. Blaszczyk, it could come in through Ms. Gallagher. It could come in through Mr. Bajagic, if he comes back. It could come in through General Zivanovic. It could come in through Petar Salapura, who is depicted in one of these videos. It could come in through a -- from a number of sources, but I think given the scheduling, the timing of the presentation of evidence that this is an appropriate avenue for which -- to introduce the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge Nyambe has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Vanderpuye, you have answered the question I was going to put to, that you are just taking us in a roundabout way through the witness hopefully something that you would be able to give us through, according to this witness's evidence, Mr. Tomasz Blaszczyk.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Blaszczyk, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Yes. I thought that would have been the appropriate witness in view of the fact that what you are trying to do here, which is correct, is to establish the chain of custody because it is him who had links with the actual people who gave him -- it gives us difficult -- for example, this witness was saying the other person in the video in a white shirt is a waiter. Now, he was not at that function, and the video does not confirm to me that that person is a waiter because a waiter would come and serve you drinks and go, but that one is there throughout. So those are some of the difficulties we have, but I -- I agree you can go with this -- this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I appreciate your observation, Your Honour, and I would point out also that this is excerpt of the -- of the larger video. There is more footage which shows the service of drinks, it shows a benediction by this priest or bishop, and -- which would put some of Mr. Janc's testimony, I think, in better context. But the video itself is quite lengthy, and I think in order to establish that context it would take, well, a substantial amount of time in order to -- in order to do that. But certainly Mr. Janc's conclusions, and I don't want to testify, but they're not without foundation in the context of the broader video. But I do appreciate it, because I appreciate your concern, because you can't see that on the video. And perhaps can I elicit this information from Mr. Janc with respect to the other videos I will show him so maybe we can have better context and you can see more directly the relevance of the conclusions that he has drawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your additional explanations, and, indeed, at a later stage we will put all these information together. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President. I think I had a document up on the screen. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, it was 6582. Thank you, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Janc, could you tell us a little bit about this document in relation to the video that we're about to see of -- regarding 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report of the Republika Srpska Ministry of Interior, crime investigation department about the search of the apartment of the Milutinovic, Milovan, conducted on 22nd July in 2009 in Banja Luka. So -- and we can see down there they have listed the items they seized during the search. And on the next page, we'll see additional ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. If we could just go to the next page briefly. All right. Can you tell us about this? These are the other items that were recovered during the course of the search?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the additional items.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And were these items delivered to the Office of the Prosecutor, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I am aware, they were all sent to the BiH State Court first, and from them, we received these items on 25th of August, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And on the 25th of August, 2009, with respect to these item, I take it you were employed by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do with the items that were received as a result of this search?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The same as for the items with the search in Belgrade, I also reviewed the DVDs and -- yeah, the DVDs which were seized with this search.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President I would offer this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1019.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show the witness 65 ter 6581, and we can get through this one just before the break, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It's acknowledgment of receipt of these documents from 25th of July, when they were taken over from the BiH State Court by our Sarajevo field office investigator, Paul Grady.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it relates to the documents which were seized during the search of Milovan Milutinovic's apartment. And we can see that there I'm referring to a reference number 02/2-19/09, dated 22nd of July, 2009, and this same reference number was referred into the report we have just seen before.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would also tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1020.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see that it's time for the break. I'd like to play the video as soon as we come back, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have to -- we must have our first break now, and we will resume at quarter past 4.00. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye, please go ahead. Oh, sorry, I didn't see that. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Peace unto this house and for all those present. May God's will be done in these proceedings and may the outcome be as God wishes not as I wish. I didn't want to exert any pressure on Mr. Vanderpuye, but I think that it would be much more appropriate to prove the authenticity of the videos through those present, that is Zivanovic, Salapura, and the others. So they are the persons that should be asked. We have nothing against bringing them. But, on the other hand, we are not opposed to using a document marked for identification. I don't want to interfere with Mr. Vanderpuye's job, but please bear in mind our position on this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. Tolimir. Before the break, we had a discussion which -- in which way, with which witness the videos should be introduced. For today, I think we have received enough explanation by Mr. Vanderpuye. You should proceed. And if there's any need about additional evidence, about their source and the content of such a video, you should consider that. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I think I have to tell you that 65 ter 6578, this, I think, is the document with the missing page has been corrected, and I think it's uploaded into e-court now. I know I that I had moved on to the second video, but I wanted to just go back just briefly for a second to the 12 July one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps there is a mistake. Are you really referring to 65 ter 6578 or 79? If I recall that correctly, the missing translation page was 65 ter 6579.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think it was -- I think it was 6578, and that was the missing page concerning the entry at -- for item number 52. I think -- so I think 6578 is correct, although you have now put some doubt in my mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which P document is it? Perhaps we can get an information from the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's P1017, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I just wanted to go back for a moment to the first video that was played, Mr. Janc. And in that video, first, you do see this priest or bishop as has been referred to. In the video itself, however, the clip that we played, we don't see him doing much, and I wondered if you could explain to the Trial Chamber what, if anything, you observed this bishop doing that's not in the frame, not in the clip that we played?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The actual tape starts with religious activity ceremony in front of the and inside the church, Orthodox church in Vlasenica, where this same bishop is having a mass there. And it continues in -- in the municipality building in Vlasenica, again, with some religious activities. So -- and this priest is involved in these activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us where the Orthodox church in Vlasenica is in relation to the -- what we can see in the video frame, which you've identified as the home of Mr. Bajagic?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Orthodox church in Vlasenica is in city centre, close to the city centre, yes. It's a -- and then municipality building is just few hundred metres away from the church, and the house, Bajagic's house, is next to the main road Vlasenica-Milici, just outside the -- the Vlasenica city centre. So when you go down towards Milici it is on the right-hand side, just next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And we've seen in the video whom you've identified as General Milenko Zivanovic was the commander of the Drina Corps on 12 July. Can you tell us what relationship the town of Vlasenica has to the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In Vlasenica, the Drina Corps is actually located, so that's the seat of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I wondered if I could invited Court if it had any other questions with respect to this particular video before I moved on to the next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: No, please move on to the next video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Now we were talking a moment ago about the 13 July video which I think we'll play now. This was 65 ter 1396.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I just stopped the frame for a moment because I was going to ask the witness to identify the individuals that are shown in this frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you could, Mr. Janc, could you tell us who -- who is depicted in this particular frame.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. First, woman from the left in white shirt, she's a Serb returning back home to Srebrenica. Behind her we just see the head of Colonel Petar Salapura, the intelligence officer of the VRS Main Staff. Next to it, we see looking on the other side is a man with blond hair. He is a body-guard of General Ratko Mladic. And we see the man in between General Ratko Mladic and this -- his body-guard, with a cap on it, he is -- he is Zvonko Bajagic. And the last man on the right-hand side, is General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I'll just play the video out and then I'll ask you a little bit more about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what -- how did you find out that these people are depicted in this still?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can. Regarding the woman, it is from the content of this video we can conclude who that woman is, although we don't know her name. For General Ratko Mladic, it's during the course of the investigation we -- we found who that -- that individual is. And for Petar Salapura, I can say I personally met him here when he was -- during his proofing session for Popovic trial, so I can identify him as being him. We also identified the body-guards when we interviewed him, not me personally, but I think for sure my colleague Blaszczyk. And for Zvonko Bajagic, I already explained, I can also identify him because, through his testimony here I know him, how he looked like, so that's how I can -- how I can identify these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We can just play out the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, Judge Nyambe has an additional question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Firstly I still have some difficulty why this video is being played with this witness. That's -- that problem still exists. Secondly, he -- he refers to the woman as wearing a shirt. I think that's a T-shirt. And there's a big difference between a T-shirt and a shirt. The least he can do is make the identification correctly. But I still have some basic difficulty why we are seeing this video -- I'm not saying it's not -- you should not introduce it, but why through this witness and not through Blaz -- whatever it is and whoever is supposed to produce -- to introduce it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand your concern. And I think it is really more a matter of -- for the moment, it's a matter of convenience and opportunity in order to play the videotape and introduce it before the Court. I think that Mr. Janc is just as valid a basis to introduce this video as any other witness would be because of his familiarity and involvement in the investigation and his ability to explain the context and the participants in the video themselves. I take your point with respect to the description that Mr. Janc gave concerning the woman depicted in the video. However, I think also that the video functionally speaks for itself. Mr. Janc's observations with respect to the videos are not clearly binding on the Court. The evidence that we seek to introduce is the video, the substance of the video itself. But I think that Mr. Janc's testimony is also valuable to the court in terms of orienting the Court with respect to the content of the video, the context of the video, and the people that are actually depicted in the video. In this case, you can see, even from the subtitling and from the transcript of the video, that General Mladic, for example, is identified. And so clearly Mr. Janc's identification of General Mladic is not substantive in this case because the video speaks for itself. You are right, there are other avenues in which to introduce this video. There are other mechanisms and vehicles that perhaps the Prosecution could have chosen to use, but I think fundamentally the question is whether or not there's a sufficient basis that resides in Mr. Janc to introduce it, and I think that there is because of his knowledge of the case and his involvement in analysing this material, reviewing this material, as well as his involvement or knowledge of how the material was acquired. You can imagine a certain situation where, for example, material has been turned over to the Prosecutor and the person who turned it over has died or can't be located. But it -- to the extent that there is a -- a sequence of events or chain of events that can establish the provenance of the article through somebody who has reviewed it, somebody who has experience with it, that would be also be an appropriate vehicle to introduce that piece of evidence through, as it would had the person survived and not disappeared or -- or died. So I think that that's an appropriate basis upon which to -- to introduce the evidence. As I mentioned before, this particular video features Colonel Petar Salapura, who Mr. Janc has identified as an intelligence officer, in fact the chief of intelligence, in the VRS Main Staff. He's on our witness list, we expect him to testify, and, hopefully, we expect to be able to play this videotape to him and to have him identify himself to the court, which I think would probably be the most straightforward authentication of this material, but I don't think it's the only course of action is my point and that's the reason why I think it is appropriate to address the matter through Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: At the moment we are not in the position to decide about admission of this video into evidence. We look at it, and this witness is only in the position to testify about his investigation, how he took part in the investigation, and the methods he used during his investigation because he was not an eye-witness and he was not on the spot at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Could you just bear with me for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Mr. McCloskey has reminded me that Mr. Janc has just testified he actually met with Colonel Salapura and he is identifying on his -- identifying based on his own personal knowledge on -- of having seen him. So that's clearly, I think, a sufficient basis in and of itself to identify this witness -- identify or authenticate this tape. He is in the best position to do that because he has personally met Colonel Salapura. Colonel Salapura's presence in and around Srebrenica on the 13th of July, 1995, is obviously a significant issue in this case. It's relevant given his relationship to the accused in this case, his subordination to the accused in this case, and the events in the context of the events that were occurring in and around that area on -- on that date and thereafter. So I think that there is a sufficient basis certainly under Rule 85 for the admission of the tape, A, as it -- I think its reliability can be established through the witness and clearly its relevancy to the events in question under the indictment is rather direct. So I wanted to add that as well. And I think -- I think that that is a sufficient basis for its admission even at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye, again, we are not in a position to decide that now. We want to see the whole video. And we would be happy, if you could, distinguish while putting questions to the witness if he personally know -- knows and recognises a person depicted in the video or if he knows it from his investigation by comparing videos with other videos. It is important to know what is the source of his personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Otherwise, we are only on the position to mark it for identification. This video, if you want to use it with another witness, for instance, witness Salapura, you may do that. At the moment we are not deciding on that. We wait for the end of this video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. President. The video is, I think, only a couple of seconds more, so we'll play it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. That's the end of the video. I would like to revisit the issue of its admissibility obviously now that it is concluded. But there is one issue that I wanted to address and that was -- I forgot to mention this earlier, is that I realize now that the subtitles are all in English, and I understand that we have not received or we are not receiving any French interpretation of the transcript of the video. We've asked for that -- we've asked that that not be the case because it would interfere with the audio and even if the language is different the tenor of the conversation, the cadence of the conversation, all of this can affect the evidence. But I would like to ask whether or not this poses a problem for -- for the Bench not to have the availability of -- of French translation at this time, if can we can proceed as we have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: Yes, I checked. I was receiving the French interpretation of the document. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This problem is solved. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes it is. And that's good. What I'd like to do then is I'd like to tender this video into evidence on the basis that I have articulated before. It's 1396.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think the Chamber would like to postpone the decision about admission of this document. We have to consider your submission on that, but we will mark it for identification so that we know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I would like to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 1396 will be Exhibit P1021, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd like to move to the next one, and that's a video that we have here indicating 16 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you have familiarity with this particular video?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. I also reviewed this video. And it -- it shows it's happening in Belgrade in military hospital on 16th of July. That's first part of the video. With General Ratko Mladic present, some doctors from the hospital, and a delegation from the -- Canada, and those members are the members of the humanitarian organisation Serbian Republic from Canada. So and they brought -- they donated a medical scanner to this military hospital in Belgrade at that time. So General Ratko Mladic is there, and later on, we see, the day after, on 17 of July, the video from -- from Han -- from Crna Rijeka actually, with General Ratko Mladic inside the -- the facilities, military facilities there, together with General Milan Gvero, and also the same Canadian group of people is present when discussing. And we obtained this video --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we move into private session please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to adjourn, and we will resume at quarter past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President. I think we've -- I think we've pretty much concluded with the last videotape, which was 65 ter 5508, which I will have tendered at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But we will not receive it now but only marked for identification. We still are concerned about the question of this witness is the right one through -- if this document should be -- the video should be received through this witness. It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1022, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I did want to point out that it's my understanding that the Defence does not have an objection to the admission of the videos themselves, at least they've not indicated that to us, and I think I've approached them with respect to whether or not they had any objections to any of the documents or videos that I would be using. utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber is really concerned about that, because we have checked again the summary from our -- from your 65 ter witness list, and we don't see anything about videos to be shown but only results of exhumations of the Srebrenica-related mass graves and the collection of human remains from the surface, so in that way we are really concerned why these videos are shown with this witness. But we shouldn't waste court time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will decide that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understand. You're referring to the 65 ter witness summary. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Exactly. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. President. What I'd like to deal with now --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, is P681, and we'll get that up hopefully in a moment. But this is a video that is dated 21 July 1995. And do you have any familiarity with this particular video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do have. I also reviewed this video, and it is the farewell or leaving the DutchBat Srebrenica enclave on 21st of July.
