utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: For the record, could you please repeat from whom you received that. It is not included in the record it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can. It is Antelope Production.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know, based upon your review of the information concerning this video footage, from where the Antelope Production Company secured this video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately. There was just information on our note that when did we get this -- this footage from, but no further information from where they -- they got this -- this video from.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know for whom this particular production was being prepared; that is, "The Cry From The Grave"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. If I'm not wrong, it was for -- it was first -- no, I cannot comment on that. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Have you had an opportunity to review the footage yourself?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, several times, that I can confirm, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that in the course of your functions as an investigator in the Srebrenica case, separate and apart from your preparation for your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us approximately, if you can remember, how many times you might have -- you might have actually reviewed this footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say around three to four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And in the context of your involvement in the investigation, were you able to individual any particular individuals that are featured in this video footage?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. There are the Dutch Battalion military officials there on this footage. And I can start with DutchBat battalion in Srebrenica, commander Lieutenant-Colonel Thomas Karremans. And also General Nicolai Cornelis who has testified here in this case already, he is on that video. And several others, other DutchBat battalion members you can see on this video. Apart from that, also the members of the VRS are present on this video, starting with General Ratko Mladic, there is also Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic, the Drina Corps -- Drina Corps security officer, and, of course, there is also Colonel Radoslav Jankovic; he is the intelligence officer of the VRS Main Staff. Apart from that, we can also see, I think, the member of the state security from Serbia, which I don't think we know who he actually is, but from the video itself, you can -- you can hear that -- that is he from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thanks for that. I think we can get started and play that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's 65 ter -- I'm sorry. It's P681.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I just wanted to stop for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If you can identify who we have in the frame here, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. On the left-hand side turned with a back to us, it is General Ratko Mladic. On the right-hand side, with a blue beret, it is General Nicolai Cornelis. And I cannot recognise who that individual behind the General Cornelis is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of your identity of General Cornelis Nicolai in the right-hand of this frame, right-hand side of this frame, can you tell us what the basis of your knowledge is for that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Nicolai testified here for this trial and also before for Popovic trial, and I was personally present when we proofed him for Popovic trial, so I met him personally and I know that's him for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. We can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should indicate the time when you stopped the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're right. Thank you Mr. President. That's at 00 minutes, 35 seconds. And I think we can go on a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us who this individual is now that's in the frame and the blue beret? And that's at 47 seconds in this video.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is Lieutenant-Colonel Thomas Karremans. He was the commander of the Dutch battalion in Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what's the basis of your knowledge for that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't met him personally, but I know he was identified several times during -- when I was present during the proofing sessions with Dutch -- Dutch Battalion personnel who came here to testify in Popovic and also in this Tolimir trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you seen him before in the context of any other video footage that you may have reviewed?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. He is also present at all these three Fontana meetings in Bratunac, and also through the course of reviewing these videos and other stuff, I can be -- I can confirm that that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. I've interrupted it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, are you able to identify the individual on the left side of this frame? And that's at 2 minutes 30 seconds in this footage.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the first individual from the far left side with blond hair, that's the body-guard of General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And can you tell us what the basis of your knowledge is for that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same -- the basis for my knowledge is that I got aware who that individual is during the -- as a member of him being involved in the investigative activities in relation to Srebrenica, and I learned that this guy, this individual, through statements that he is the body-guard of General Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is he featured in any of the videos we've seen today?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is. He is individual who was present together with Ratko Mladic on 13 of July in Srebrenica in that house with woman refugee. He is present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. I think we can -- we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We are at 2 minutes and 58 seconds in this frame. Can you tell us -- well, can you identify any of the individuals here.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The first individual from the left-hand side is the same as before, so a body-guard of the General Ratko Mladic. The individual next to it, to his left, I don't recognise. And then the third one, which is from our left-hand side or just behind General Ratko Mladic, is Lieutenant-Colonel Vujadin Popovic, the Drina Corps chief of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what's your basis of knowledge with respect to your identification of Lieutenant-Colonel Popovic in this frame?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was one of the accused in -- in so-called Popovic et al case, so that's the main source. And also, throughout the investigation we came across his name and footages with him being on -- on this footage -- footages. Very often also many people identified him on these footages. So that's my knowledge of -- of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think we can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, we have an indication here that this was on 21 July. Are you able to confirm that? And if you can, can you tell us what the basis for that is.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, this is 21st of July, when the DutchBat left the enclave and we can -- we can get this information -- actually, I got this information from several documents in relation to our investigation, I'm including the witnesses's statements and documents from VRS and UNPROFOR sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And at the very beginning of the -- or near the beginning of the footage we see a bridge. Can you orient the Trial Chamber and tell us where that is in relation to the -- to the -- to the departure of the Dutch Battalion?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This is actually in Bratunac and the bridge goes over the Drina River into Serbia. And DutchBat was situated in Potocari which is just few kilometres away from Bratunac or from the spot we have seen here on this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put an additional question. Have you ever been in Bratunac or Potocari.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, indeed. I've been in Bratunac several times, also in Potocari several times. But I can confirm I've never been at this particular spot, what we see on this video. So at this border crossing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There is just one other person I'd like you to take a look at to see if you can identify, and I think we have it here. It's at 41 seconds in this video. Are you able to recognise the individual next to General Nicolai with the -- appears to be a brown beret on.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This is individual which I was not sure before who that was. But now I can recognise him. He is Colonel Radoslav Jankovic, the officer of the intelligence department of the VRS Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you know off the top of your head what his relationship was to Colonel Petar Salapura, the chief of intelligence of the VRS Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This individual, Colonel Jankovic, was subordinated to him directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would tender this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is it already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, then I don't tender it. I do have an another video that I would like to play. It's -- it's longer than the time that we have left and I think it would be better to proceed with it tomorrow, with leave of the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And so I would like, with leave of the Court, to end today. I expect -- I have three more videos to go through tomorrow. At the pace that it's going, I hope it will improve, but I expect at this pace it will take up most of tomorrow also. But -- so that's my application. Mr. McCloskey would like to -- to address the Court briefly before we adjourn, if -- if -- if that's what is convenient for the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But how much time do you indicate we will need with the examination-in-chief of Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I may have indicated originally about the full day today. I think I'm probably going to need two sessions tomorrow to get through all of it. We have about a 20-minute video and another video, I think that the next two are about 17 minutes altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm told I'm mistaken. It's been an hour altogether video footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could consider overnight the question, if you should show these videos with this witness or not. Perhaps you could consider the question if there are more appropriate witnesses who can have more first knowledge about the source, the people who are depicted in it, and so on. You said you have different ways you could show the videos with, and, therefore, you should consider this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We'll take that under advisement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think the witness should probably leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, indeed. Mr. Janc, thank you for your attendance today again. As you see, it is a quite long story with your evidence. I'm sure -- we are sure you can't finish by tomorrow, because Mr. Tolimir will have the right to cross-examine you, and, therefore, I just want to remind you it is not allowed to have any contact with either party about the content of your testimony. Thank you very much for your attendance, and now you are free to return to your normal activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good-bye. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I just wanted to respond to a little bit of what your concerns and try to take my comments of yesterday and try to help sort out where we are. As you know we have a two-day gap and that's why this witness and this material is here. I was -- Mr. Thayer informed me that the main reason for that gap, which I didn't understand at the time, was that the first estimate that we got from the accused was -- for my witness Wright was four to five days because he was the first -- the first forensic archeology witness, and that's what Mr. Thayer based the schedule on mostly. And then, of course, as the accused reviewed the material, like we all do, and they've changed that to three to four hours. So we had this gap. And we had not originally planned on a detailed process regarding this video for you. It's never in the years that we've put on this video has anyone ever objected to it. All the accused have always -- no one's ever objected to any of the people or authentication in it, which would come out, whether you take that as any value. I understand you're a new Bench and you may not hold much stock in that, but as we learned that you want details on this, of course, we also never got any objection from General Tolimir on this video, and he knows these -- the evidence will show he knows these people. So -- but as we began to learn that you wanted more on this, then we started thinking, well, we need to get the investigators ready to do this, and it came a little bit earlier than we thought. And when I look at the 65 ter summaries for the investigators, it was Erin Gallagher that we had put down as our video person because she had some knowledge in the videos. However, Dusan Janc is probably the best investigator and the best person to do this work. The best example that you saw today is he spent an entire proofing session with Colonel Salapura, and this -- the issue of Colonel Salapura identified with General Mladic on 13 July in Srebrenica is very important. There is no better witness than -- than Mr. Janc to identify Salapura. Salapura, himself, Your Honours, as you will see was involved in these events. We haven't shown him that video as we got it relatively recently, but he could, I don't think so, but he could get up and say, "That's not me," but I would argue that Dusan Janc's identification will be better than that. Mr. Bajagic testified in this trial and is not a reliable witness in my view. Dusan Janc is a much better witness than Bajagic, and I am convinced that you would see that had you seen that. So we don't put Dusan Janc up here half heartedly or without preparation. He reads the language. He understands what's being said when he sees these videos. He's got a good memory, and he on short notice is one of the best people to do that. He didn't drive around quite as much as Mr. Blaszczyk who ends up signing these things, but Mr. Blaszczyk would bring it to him. These people, Gallagher, Blaszczyk, and Janc are in the same office about 2 metres from each other, so he really is an excellent witness for this material. And there is the -- the legal issue here is we don't have an objection, we have material that speaks for itself. I mean, this is amazing material that would be very difficult to fake. We've all seen fakes, so we understand your skepticism and we will meet that with the evidence. But it does speak for itself. Remember that. And it's a question of admissibility. Admissibility with the basics of how we got it, that should make it admissible under the law here. Admissibility is a very low threshold. Now, the weight that you give it, that's what we're talking about. So we would argue that this material is clearly admissible based that we got and when we got it and how we got it. How much weight you give it is, of course, your determination. So we believe that this is more of a weight issue than an admissibility issue. However, I'm very happy that are you questioning this so that we know now that you need the answers to these questions. And so we will provide you as best we can with the answers through Mr. Janc and through the other -- the other people. But just so you know, for example, the -- the last -- the last video of the departure of the DutchBat from iron bridge, you will be hearing from Sergeant Major Rave. He was there, he was a part of it. He'll recognise all the Dutch people. He'll recognise some of the Serbian People that was in it. So he'll -- he's going to be able to put that in context for you if we need it. Major Boering, who is also our witness, will be able to do it. And Colonel Salapura has testified here, he's co-operated, and I expect he will testify, and I do expect him to actually acknowledge that's him in Srebrenica. But you never know. And so where we can we're bringing you people that were actually in the video, you're going to see documents associated with the videos, and it's a very colourful group of people, and it's certainly not just Mr. Janc. And now that we know, you know, how important it is for you, these details, we're going to churn up these details more and remember these videos better for all the other witnesses. But you will see from a lot of these people that are in this video you get to see. But Mr. Janc is -- is a great witness for this. There is no better from the investigative team. Much of this material came in after Mr. Ruez was here, and we -- we had given this some thought, though it wasn't on the description, we put the description for that in Erin Gallagher. And Erin Gallagher, there is another exhibit that goes along with all these videos. It's basically the -- this booklet, and this booklet is a booklet of stills, and -- sorry, I don't have the 65 ter number for it right now. It has one, of course. And basically it's a series of important stills and Erin Gallagher is right now preparing to testify about these stills. As you may recall Mr. Janc saying that she was going testify about who is who in these videos, and this particular document lists some of the things that support how the investigation has identified various people, and so it's basically the playbook. Not that our videos are an opera, but it's critical to the -- to the video you'll see to have the playbook so that when you go back and take a look at these videos you will this in front of you that will say who people are. And -- but we're not asking you just to count on the investigators for this. We will throughout this trial you will see over and over again who these people are, and I have every confidence that General Tolimir, if we get anybody wrong, will let us know, as he should do as representing his Defence. I know we don't expect any statements from him but as he represents his Defence, if we get something wrong, I'm sure he will tell us. But in any event, I've talked for too long now, but that's -- that's what I wanted to tell you about, the whole picture. Yes, we've come in not as prepared as we would like, but this is -- these are reliable folks, and we appreciate your questions because we were -- this is new for us. It's a new panel and every panel is different and we know that and we appreciate that and we respect it, so we are very happy that you are asking questions now and that we don't find out down the road. So thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. McCloskey, for your thoughtful comments. I think that was helpful for the Chamber to receive your position and we will consider that as well. I will not comment on that now. But you must understand that, indeed, every Chamber is a separate chamber in this Tribunal, as everywhere in the world, and we have to make our own Judgement at the end of the day, and we are not saying anything about the qualification of any witness here. We will do that at the end of the day. But we understand your position, and we have listened carefully. Thank you very much for that. Mr. Tolimir, do you want to respond? You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I don't have anything to say. Tomorrow is another day, and I don't want to keep you any longer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then we are expecting another interesting day of hearing tomorrow. We have to adjourn now and resume tomorrow at 9.00 in this courtroom.
